Subject: Workload profile & dedicated sizing — GPU tier, TPS, token mix (recap + asks)

Thanks for the call earlier, Ethan/Alyssa — quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets your availability and cost targets.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: real-time chat + summary generation for customer support.
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for short requests; p95 <= 400ms acceptable for long summaries.
- Traffic shape: baseline ~40 TPS with frequent business-hour spikes (you mentioned peaks).
- Token mix (estimate): ~70% short (10–40 tokens), ~30% long (800–1,500 tokens) — please confirm.
- Model: open LLM family (we discussed LlamaX-13B / finetuned variant).
- Compliance: SOC 2 + customer audit readiness (you flagged procurement review).

Internal recommendation (short): Dedicated reserved pool is the cleanest fit given latency and compliance needs; burst capacity off-hosted for peak smoothing. Two GPU families to consider:
- A10G (cost-efficient, good for higher multiplexing, works well with quantized 8-bit pipelines)
- H100 (higher single-request throughput and lower latency for long-token requests; higher cost)

Concrete asks / next steps
1) Please confirm realistic token distribution (short vs long) and a 48-hour representative request log if available — I've attached a CSV template (sentrydata_poc_profile.csv).
2) Confirm burst profile: baseline vs typical peak duration (e.g., 30–90s) and daily peak windows.
3) Do you need Private (VPC/on-prem) for this PoC, or is Dedicated (VPC-enabled) sufficient to satisfy procurement?
4) We propose a 60–90 minute sizing workshop next week (we'll bring rough throughput math).

I've attached the CSV template for the request-profile and will follow up with a back-of-envelope configuration and cost delta (A10G vs H100) after you confirm token mix.

Thanks,
Maya

Thanks, Maya — appreciate the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- Token distribution: your estimate is close. Roughly 65–70% short (<40 tokens), 25% medium (40–400 tokens), ~5–10% long (>800 tokens) for deep summaries. We'll pull a 48-hour sample and drop it in your CSV.
- Traffic spikes: baseline 35–45 TPS; spikes to ~180–220 TPS for 30–90 seconds (around product release windows and customer mornings). Spikes are predictable but frequent.

Chiming in with a rough starting configuration / math so we can answer Ethan's cost & concurrency asks quickly. This is high-level — we'll refine after we get the 48-hour profile.

Assumptions from Maya's recap + Ethan's clarification:
- Baseline steady-state ~40 TPS.
- Spike target: 220 TPS sustained for ~60s.
- Model: LlamaX-13B (quantized 8-bit works for most short requests; long-summary path may need float16 or H100-accelerated precision).
- Effective throughput (estimate):
  * A10G: ~60–80 short-request TPS per GPU when multiplexed (8–12 concurrent streams), long requests reduce throughput dramatically (estimated 6–12 long-request TPS per GPU)
  * H100: ~130–180 short-request TPS per GPU and ~30–50 long-request TPS per GPU (better at long-context memory ops)

Back-of-envelope pools to cover spikes without cold provisioning (target: keep queueing minimal):
- A10G path: 4–6 A10G GPUs (reserved) + hosted burst capacity for transient spikes -> covers baseline and mild spikes; cost-efficient if 70% work is short tokens.
- H100 path: 2 H100 GPUs (reserved) with a smaller hosted fallback for extreme concurrency; fewer GPUs but higher hourly cost.

Concurrency / KV-cache notes:
- For short-chat UX, small concurrency per model instance (8–12) with prefix KV cache reduces repeated context cost.
- For long summaries, pin to H100 or a CPU offload for pre/post-processing to avoid tokenization latency spikes.

Estimated monthly delta (very rough):
- A10G reserved + burst: baseline committed cost X (we'll put numbers in the quote).
- H100 reserved + burst: ~2.5–3x the committed monthly compute cost but reduces latency and GPU count.

Next actions for us (Maya/Priyom)
1) Produce a short 1-page PoC sizing table (A10G vs H100 scenarios) and attach an updated quote (done).
2) Confirm whether you want us to size for minimal cost (A10G-first) or minimal latency (H100-first) for the PoC.
3) Prep a 60–90 minute sizing workshop after we receive the sample logs.

I've attached an updated quote PDF (redwood_dedicated_quote_v2.pdf) for the two scenarios — please do not circulate outside SentryData procurement until we finalize numbers.

Ben
